last.summary: It didn't come together this time. The trace below says why, and most of it says when.

crew.name: Kev
crew.about: Lead. Fourteen years. Steady and fast, carries more than his share. The crew asks him before they ask you.

crew.name: Lyle
crew.about: Fit-up. Six years. Careful and quiet; the best jig man in the plant. Says little in huddles.

crew.name: Brent
crew.about: Body weld. Four years. A strong welder and a loud one. The crew likes him. Late sometimes.

crew.name: Marisol
crew.about: Body weld. Two years. Precise, improving fast, asks good questions. Hard on herself.

crew.name: Tyler
crew.about: Body weld. Nine months. Quick hands, quick to rush. Three small rework tickets last month.

crew.name: Donna
crew.about: Finish and inspect. Eleven years. Sees everything and tells you most of it. Kev's peer, not always his friend.

crew.name: Joel
crew.about: Finish and inspect. Three months. New, keen, hesitates. Trained by Donna, watched by everyone.

lines.text: 7 bodies went over to paint. They asked for 6.
It's the motor. The bearing's on its way out.
Kev called in Monday and stayed out 3 days.
The haze at booth three was there again by mid-morning.
Paint got 6 bodies against the 6 they wanted.
You walked the work order over to maintenance yourself and stood there until it went on the board.
Tyler took his hood off at booth three on Thursday and you could see the haze around him.
About 45 hours this week, which is a normal week by most standards and a light one by yours.

decisions.note: Went and looked when someone raised safety
Kept a promise to HR and the crew

cards.title: Your standing week
cards.body: The things that happen every week whether or not anything else does. Each one you skip saves the hours and costs something quieter.

items.label: Production meeting
items.why: Dana runs it Tuesdays. Skip it and she hears about your week from someone else.

items.label: Jess's capacity numbers
items.why: Jess builds next week from them. Skip it and next week holds a surprise.

items.label: Safety walk
items.why: Thursday, with the checklist. Skip it and nobody looks.

items.label: Timecards
items.why: Payroll needs them by Friday, and they are where lateness shows up.

items.label: Paint handoff
items.why: Ten minutes a day at the paint door. Skip it and more of your rework goes over.

items.label: Morning huddles
items.why: Five minutes a day with the crew. Skip them and the day starts without a plan.

cards.title: The extractor at booth three
cards.body: Booth three's extractor still isn't pulling right. Tyler's started propping the door.
know: The motor's bearing is going. It's still turning, slower than it should.
Tried: walk the work order over to maintenance. It has not held.

options.label: Go and look at it now
Put in a maintenance work order
Walk the work order over to maintenance
Shut booth three until it is fixed
Move Tyler to another booth for now

cards.title: Theresa wants half an hour
cards.body: Two bodies went over Monday with spatter in the drip rail. Theresa wants half an hour, and she would like it today.

cards.title: Engineering wants a welder to look at a drawing
cards.body: Ben in manufacturing engineering has a revised fixture for the Drayman Crew cab and wants a welder's eye on it before it goes to the toolroom. An hour and a half at his bench. He asked nicely, which with Ben means it matters.

options.label: Go and look at it with him

effects.line: You found a clamp that sits right where the torch has to go on the B-pillar seam. Ben took the drawing back and thanked you twice.

score: Gave engineering a welder before it was too late

options.label: Tell him it looks fine from here

queue.line: The new Drayman Crew fixture arrived. The clamp on the B-pillar seam sits right where the torch has to go, and the welds there show it.

cards.title: The gas supplier wants a call
cards.body: The gas supplier wants an hour to 'review the account'. Purchasing owns the account.

cards.title: An hour with someone
cards.body: Nobody is asking for this. An hour at someone's station, showing and watching, is how people get better between the times something goes wrong.

cards.title: Weld a booth yourself
cards.body: The booths look good for about 6.5 bodies this week. Paint wants 6. You could still pick up a stinger, and every day you do is a day of your own work that waits.

cards.title: Walk the floor
cards.body: Two hours a week, no clipboard, just walking the bay and talking to people. It's how you find out what the timecards and the QC tickets won't tell you.
